name: the-docked-sidebar-keeps-its-glass-after-a-reveal
description:
The reporter's DOCKED sidebar paints as an opaque slab while the surround band beside it still shows the glass, on a profile with the opacity at 30%. Both are the same window and the same backdrop, so something covers the sidebar column alone.

The suspect is the handover. The sidebar's WebContents is made transparent ONCE, when it is built (atrium_browser_window.cc:4895) - rwhv->SetBackgroundColor plus SetPageBaseBackgroundColor. Revealing the panel moves that WebContents to a second views::WebView and docking moves it back, and neither HandSidebarToPanel nor DockFloatingSidebar re-applies either. A RenderWidgetHostView rebuilt across that move comes back with the default opaque background, and the renderer then paints over the window's own backdrop.

This is why the VM said nothing before: A fresh profile's 0xB8 tint hides the docked frost in both arms. The settings fixture here carries the reporter's own 30%, so the frost is visible and a slab is not.

The reading is a before and after of the SAME docked sidebar, either side of one reveal-and-dock cycle. Nothing about the sidebar should differ.

actions.expression: (() => { const l = document.querySelector('.bglayer'); if (!l) return 'no-bglayer'; const r = l.getBoundingClientRect(); return getComputedStyle(l).backgroundImage.slice(0, 120) + ' @ ' + Math.round(r.width) + 'x' + Math.round(r.height); })()
actions.note: installSkylight paints a base of linear-gradient(165deg, #14181D, #0B0D10) - opaque - into this layer on every sidebar paint. If it is there and sized, no glass opacity can show the desktop through it.
